mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% in a month signals aggressive Fed easing, lowering real rates and boosting equity present value, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day pre-trigger average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising PAYEMS (labor market strength) coinciding with UNRATE below 4% predicts a tight labor market that supports corporate hiring and consumer demand, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE remains below 4% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Tight labor market with low unemployment
failure_condition: 60-day returns under trigger regime are negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST (industrial production) above 1% suggests accelerating output growth, which anticipates higher future earnings and pushes 20-day S&P 500 returns positive.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in all 12 months following the expansion phase (rolling mean p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) index below 110 signals supply-side weakness, reducing future earnings expectations and producing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in 80% of INDPRO < 110 months (rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL inflation exceeding 2% for two consecutive months triggers a preemptive rate hike anticipation, compressing equity valuations and driving negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during inflation spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 3.5% combined with rising PAYEMS indicates a shift from labor market weakness to strength, boosting investor confidence and supporting positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% while PAYEMS increases over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day returns under this regime are flat or negative (mean ratio ≤ 1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in GDPC1 (GDP) above -1% suggest economic softness, lowering growth expectations and producing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.05) during softening periods.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both INDPRO and HOUST for three months indicate supply and demand both weakening, amplifying earnings downgrades and yielding negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
regime_hint: Dual softening in output and activity
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in 70% of such dual softening windows (rolling window).
